name: arxiv-slop
title: Templatedness (arXiv 2509.19163)
description: One rule, for the one code in the paper's taxonomy that this engine can genuinely own. Shaib, Chakrabarty, Garcia-Olano and Wallace define eleven codes; five need human annotation and the paper reports that reasoning models fail at extracting them too. SQ2 Templatedness is the exception: the paper measures it via syntactic structures, and so does this.

rules.name: Repeated syntactic frame
rules.description: Three or more consecutive sentences built on the same syntactic frame, with different words in the slots. The paper's own example is a run of “Dr. Smith, a researcher at Oxford University, found that…”. The `echo` detector cannot see this, because every content word differs; what repeats is the shape. Content words are wildcarded and only the closed class is compared, so the badge shows the frame that repeated.
rules.suggest: Vary the sentence shapes, or collapse the run into one sentence and a list. Three identical frames read as a form someone filled in.
rules.note: A crude stand-in for part-of-speech tagging, which this engine does not have. It found zero false positives in 30,300 words of human technical prose, but the guard doing most of that work is the requirement that a frame contain at least two closed-class anchors — without it, code and table rows match each other.

hit: Dr. Smith, a researcher at Oxford University, found that the effect was small. Professor Johnson, a scientist at Cambridge University, discovered that it held. Dr. Williams, an expert at Yale University, confirmed that the result was real.
The first phase focuses on discovery and stakeholder alignment. The second phase focuses on design and technical validation. The third phase focuses on delivery and operational handover.
miss: The parser is fast. We rewrote it last spring after the incident that took the queue down for a morning. Nobody has touched it since, which is probably for the best.
Dr. Smith found that the effect was small. The team at Cambridge could not reproduce it. A third group tried a different measure entirely and gave up.
